summary.text: Upwelling is the wind-driven rise of dense, cool, usually nutrient-rich deep water to the ocean surface, where it replaces warmer surface water.
Wind, the Coriolis effect and Ekman transport work together to move surface water, and where that water spreads apart, deep water rises to replace it.
The nutrients feed phytoplankton, so five upwellings covering only 5% of the ocean supply about 25% of the world's marine fish catch.

facts.label: Main drivers
facts.value: Wind, Coriolis effect and Ekman transport

facts.label: Telltale signs
facts.value: Cool surface water and high chlorophyll a

items.prompt: Upwelling zones are small. Five of them cover only about 5% of the ocean. Roughly what share of the world's marine fish catch do those five supply?

options.label: About 1%
About 5%
About 25%
About 90%

items.explain: About a quarter of global marine fish catches come from five upwellings that occupy just 5% of the ocean.

items.prompt: Why do fishing fleets gather where cold deep water rises to the surface?

options.label: Its nutrients feed phytoplankton, the base of the food chain
Cold water slows the fish down so they are easier to catch
Strong winds herd fish into tight schools near the coast
The rising water lifts schools of fish up from the deep seafloor

items.explain: Nutrients boost phytoplankton growth, and that high primary production passes up the food chain to fish.

items.prompt: In the Northern Hemisphere, a steady wind blows across the sea. Overall, which way does the surface water end up moving?

options.label: Straight along with the wind
At right angles, to the left of the wind
Directly back against the wind
At right angles, to the right of the wind

items.explain: Coriolis forces and Ekman transport move the water a net 90 degrees from the wind, to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.

items.prompt: There is no Coriolis force right at the equator. Can upwelling still happen near it?

options.label: No, it always needs the Coriolis force
Yes, just north and south of the equator
Only during rare El Niño years
Only right beside a stretch of coastline

items.explain: Upwelling still occurs just north and south of the equator, where the water diverges.

items.prompt: A researcher scans ocean maps looking for upwelling zones. Which combination gives one away?

options.label: Warm surface water with lots of chlorophyll
Cool surface water with little chlorophyll
Cool surface water with lots of chlorophyll
Warm surface water with little chlorophyll

items.explain: Cool rising water plus thriving phytoplankton show up as low surface temperatures and high chlorophyll a.

items.prompt: Wind and Earth's spin push surface water away from one stretch of sea, so the water there spreads apart. What happens next?

options.label: The surface water there freezes
Rain slowly refills the gap
Surface water sinks to make room
Deep water rises to fill the gap

items.explain: When the net movement of water diverges, deep water wells up to replace what was lost.
